minutes.headline: Sewer Commission voted to send a grease-trap non-compliance letter to Il Forno and asked staff to price E1 pumps for Upland/White Street.
minutes.summary: The commission discussed the Upland/White Street sewer extension, weighing low-pressure E1 grinder pumps against gravity lines, and directed a member to research pump pricing and arrange an engineer visit. It approved two sets of minutes, voted to start a grease-trap non-compliance process against one restaurant, and acknowledged invoices. The commission also discussed Green Communities grant ideas, such as solar panels at pump stations, and the town meeting warrant, including a citizen petition to expand the sewer area.

A non-compliant business is charged a fee, which reverts to a daily rate back to the non-compliance date if the report is not filed by April 7.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted by roll call to send a non-compliance letter to Il Forno over an overdue grease trap report; the vote tally was not audible.
On the Upland/White Street extension, John Reynolds is to ask the local E1 sales rep about pump availability and prices, and a resident Q&A was proposed.
The commission will invite the Wright-Pierce engineer to a meeting to answer questions on the Upland/White Street proposal.
The commission backed putting solar panels at pump stations forward for a Green Communities grant, and Bob is to tell the Green Committee.
A 40B project update goes on the next agenda, and meetings stay remote through April.

why_it_matters: The Upland/White Street choice between gravity lines and low-pressure grinder pumps decides what connection costs fall on the households on those streets, and no customer cost figure was given at this meeting.
A business that misses the grease trap reporting deadline is charged a fee that becomes a daily rate back to the non-compliance date, so a late filing costs more over time.
watch_next: The next Sewer Commission meeting: the engineer's visit on Upland/White Street, the E1 pump pricing, and the 40B update.
The April 7 grease trap report deadline, after which the daily fee applies back to the non-compliance date.
